items.quote: Star Wars Galactic Racer is a Star-Wars-authentic thrill rush that may be the best racer in a decade. It’s such a wonderful, engaging experience that literally does everything right. Just be warned – as a roguelite – the on-ramp can take time while presenting a higher difficulty level.

Star Wars Galactic Racer is the perfect racing game. Fast, furious and frenetic gameplay makes every corner and turn feel such a matter of life or death. A superb unique campaign full of great characters and moments, addictive gameplay loops and a plethora of content make this a game for the ages. The first time you podrace will stay in my memory forever, like being transported into the films. It will take some doing for this game to be displaced as my game of the year. In a year of heavyweight developers flexing their muscles, it’s a brand new team from Guildford who have captured my attention. Fuse Games, congratulations on a superb effort. Besides the fact I dream of yet more planets and tracks, this is the ultimate Star Wars racer. I already long for a sequel!

What a surprise this Star Wars Galactic Racer is. Right from its initial releases, it looked promising, but now that we’ve put it through its paces for a long time, we’re even more surprised by the overall quality Fuse Games title. A delightful mix of Burnout and F-Zero, spiced up with roguelite elements that aren’t intrusive at all, in fact they raise the bar for fun even higher. With the exception of a few tracks "reading" issues - which, with practice, tend to resolve themselves anyway - we’re looking at one of the best arcade racing games of recent years: fun, challenging, and rock-solid in both single-player and multiplayer… a must play for Star Wars fans and everyone else.
Star Wars: Galactic Racer is one of the most exciting racers in recent memory, blending the Star Wars universe with gameplay that feels both fresh and intelligent.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer proves that a heavyweight license can still produce a game with a identity of its own, as long as it has the courage not to merely repeat the formula of the past. Fuse Games has taken a genre the industry had shelved and put it back on the track with a roguelite structure that works, a speed that takes your breath away and a care for its worlds that reminds you how a beloved universe should be treated.

A lot of things click in Galactic Racer. When you're behind the wheel, it feels awesome, but once that honeymoon phase and initial wow factor wear off, you realize Fuse Games didn't really look past the basics. The result? A solid game that's just a bit light on content at launch.[Recommended]

Star Wars: Galactic Racer scratches an itch I didn’t realize I had for this kind of stupidly fast arcade racer, largely thanks to a roguelite campaign that injects adrenaline into every run. Managing risky builds and chasing the high of that big payout makes it easy to get carried away, and even easier to crash and burn. It is repetitive in the same way a classic arcade cabinet is, but that magnetic pull remains; it leaves you frustrated for all of five minutes before you’re right back at the starting line for another tour.

Star Wars Galactic Racer combines exhilarating speed, spectacular collisions and vehicles with distinctly different handling. Its extensive customization and near-roguelite campaign bring real depth to the racing, making every risk matter. Strong visuals and sound create a particularly convincing sense of immersion in the Star Wars universe. However, repetitive environments, on-foot sections that slow the pace and several missing features hold the overall experience back. Despite these shortcomings, Fuse Games delivers a very good arcade racer, with foundations that make you eager to see the Galactic League broaden its horizons.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer combines precise arcade handling, distinct vehicle classes, and meaningful customization with a campaign built around risk, repetition, and gradual mastery. Track hazards, aggressive collisions, and the Ramjet system keep races tense, while the different vehicle types significantly change how each course is approached. The roguelite structure can become punishing, especially when unclear track design or abrupt difficulty spikes end a long run, and the lack of split-screen is a notable omission. Even so, its speed, mechanical depth, and strong audiovisual presentation give it a distinct identity among Star Wars racing games.
If you miss the days of Burnout, classic Need For Speed games, Split/Second: Velocity and BLUR, then you’ll be wonderfully surprised by Star Wars: Galactic Racer.
